findings.reason: the plan must either keep the directory argument on the shared reader or state that both callers resolve to `run_dir(run_id)`, and add the existing test to the write paths; without it the node hits a scope wall or silently changes which path is read.
findings.text: §27 says `_claim_registration_for_worker` "takes its registration instant from" `read_launch_claim` and that "Behaviour is unchanged", but the two read from different directories: `_claim_registration_for_worker(run_directory, run_id)` opens `run_directory / "claim.json"` (dispatch_launch.py:4672-4677) while `read_launch_claim(run_id)` resolves the path itself through `run_dir(run_id)` (dispatch_claims.py:944-952). Two production callers pass a spec-derived `run_directory` (dispatch_launch.py:3368 and :4559), and `tests/test_claim_grace_follows_live_launches.py:136` calls the helper directly with `(directory, run_id)`; that test file is not in §27's write paths, so a node that drops the now-unused parameter — the natural reading of "one reader" — breaks a test it is fenced out of.

findings.reason: a one-line doc refresh that does not alter the mechanism or the gate; it can be folded into another section without changing what §27 builds.
findings.text: the Why cites `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py` near line 748 as describing the record "in terms the two copies can now drift from", but that docstring says "The read belongs to the module that composes the launch" — which stops being true once the read moves to `dispatch_claims.py` — and recovery_liveness.py is absent from §27's write paths, so the comment is left stale.
